text: I am submitting this complaint regarding Citibanks contradictory   investigation, repeated restriction and closure of my accounts, and its   continued refusal to provide access to approximately {$34000.00} that Citi is   holding in my personal deposit and brokerage accounts. This matter arose from   a check issued to me from a home-equity line of credit serviced by XXXX XXXX   XXXX XXXX I am a borrower and obligor on that HELOC. The check was issued   directly to me and made payable in my name. The check was deposited into my   XXXX account. XXXX later restricted and closed my accounts after allegations   were apparently made by the other borrower on the HELOC. Although I provided   XXXX with loan documents and evidence showing that I was a borrower and that   the check had been issued to me, XXXX continued restricting my accounts and   ultimately terminated its relationship with me. On or around XXXX XXXX XXXX   XXXX transferred approximately {$25000.00} of my funds into my personal   Citibank account. Those funds remain in my Citi personal account. I also have   approximately {$9000.00} in a Citi brokerage account. Therefore, Citi is   currently holding approximately {$34000.00} belonging to me. Before XXXX   transferred the {$25000.00}, checks that I had written from my Citi business   account were returned on or around XXXX XXXX XXXX. Citi began restricting and   closing my accounts because the HELOC check had been returned unpaid.   However, the check was not counterfeit, forged, stolen, or issued without   authorization. I participated in an approximately three-hour telephone call   with a Citi fraud department supervisor . During that call, Citi conducted a   three-way conversation with XXXXXXXX XXXX XXXX. XXXX directly confirmed to   Citi that : \* The HELOC check was legitimate; \* The check had been authorized   and issued to me; \* I was a borrower or obligor associated with the HELOC; \*   The check was not fraudulent or counterfeit ; and \* The check was returned   only because the other borrower called and froze the credit line during the time   the check was being presented for payment. After receiving this confirmation   from XXXX, the Citi fraud supervisor told me that he would send my accounts   back for further review and reconsideration. Several weeks later, I received   written correspondence from Citi indicating that my accounts were being   reopened. However, when I attempted to create a username and regain access to   Citis online banking system, I discovered that the accounts had been blocked   again. When I contacted Citi, I was told that I would not receive online   access or access to my funds until I brought my business account current. I   repeatedly explained that Citi was already holding approximately {$25000.00}   in my personal account and approximately {$9000.00} in my brokerage account.   I requested that Citi permit me to transfer enough of those funds into my   business account to satisfy or substantially reduce the negative balance.   Citi refused. Citi has therefore created an impossible and coercive   situation. It is holding approximately {$34000.00} of my money, preventing me   from accessing or transferring that money, and simultaneously demanding that   I obtain additional outside funds before it will restore access to the funds   it already holds. The {$25000.00} transferred by XXXX is not being disputed   as belonging to Citi. It was transferred from my XXXX account into my Citi   personal account. It remains in my name and under Citis control.   Nevertheless, Citi will not allow me to transfer those funds from my personal   account into my business account to address the negative balance. Citi has   also refused my requests to internally apply or transfer the funds itself. As   a result, Citi has prevented me from using my own money to resolve the very   account deficiency that Citi says is preventing access. In an effort to   comply with Citis demands, I sold or pawned substantially all of my valuable   personal property. I also took out an emergency loan carrying approximately   XXXX percent interest compounded daily. Through these extraordinary measures,   I obtained approximately {$19000.00} to provide to Citi in an attempt to   bring the business account current and regain access to my accounts. Even   after I obtained those funds, Citi continued refusing to allow the remaining   balance to be addressed through a transfer from the approximately {$34000.00}   Citi already held. I have now exhausted my available resources. I have no   additional funds to provide Citi. Meanwhile, Citi continues to retain my   personal and brokerage funds and refuses to permit a reasonable internal   transfer. This situation has continued for nearly a month and a half. Citis   actions are especially concerning because : 1. Citi directly verified with   XXXX that the HELOC check was legitimate and authorized. 2. Citi was informed   that the check was returned only because the other borrower froze the credit   line after the check had been issued. 3. A Citi fraud supervisor advised me   that the matter would be reconsidered. 4. Citi subsequently sent written   correspondence stating that my accounts were being reopened. 5. Citi then   blocked the accounts again without giving me a clear explanation. 6. Citi is   holding approximately {$34000.00} in my personal and brokerage accounts. 7.   Citi refuses to allow me to transfer those funds to my business account. 8.   Citi refuses to perform the transfer itself. 9. Citi nevertheless demands   additional outside funds as a condition of restoring access. 10. Citis   refusal has forced me to sell valuables and incur an extraordinarily   expensive emergency loan. Citi has not provided a meaningful written   explanation identifying : \* Why it reversed its written decision to reopen   the accounts; \* What new information caused the accounts to be blocked again   ; \* Whether Citi still claims the HELOC check was fraudulent; \* Why   Shellpoints direct confirmation was insufficient; \* The exact amount required   to bring the business account current ; \* Why funds in my Citi personal and   brokerage accounts can not be transferred or applied; \* What legal or   contractual restriction prevents an internal transfer; \* What steps I must   complete to obtain access to the remaining funds ; or \* When Citi intends to   release my undisputed money. I recognize that a bank may investigate returned   checks and may decide whether to continue a customer relationship. However,   Citi should not be permitted to retain approximately {$34000.00} belonging to   a customer, block the customer from using those funds, refuse to internally   apply the funds toward a claimed negative balance, and then demand outside   money as the sole condition for access. Citis conduct appears unfair,   contradictory, and abusive. Citi has placed me in a financial trap in which   the bank controls more than enough money to substantially resolve the issue   but refuses to either release or apply it. The continued restriction has   caused severe financial harm, including : \* The sale and pawning of valuable   personal property; \* An emergency loan carrying approximately 10 percent   interest compounded daily ; \* Additional debt and financing costs ; \* Loss of   access to approximately {$34000.00} ; \* Inability to conduct ordinary   personal and business transactions; \* Disruption of my business operations; \*   Difficulty paying rent and basic living expenses; \* Loss of access to my Citi   brokerage funds; \* Damage to my ability to maintain or establish banking   relationships ; and \* Severe financial and emotional distress. I respectfully   request that the CFPB require Citi to take the following actions : 1.   Immediately provide access to all undisputed funds in my personal deposit and   brokerage accounts. 2. Permit me to transfer sufficient funds from my   personal or brokerage accounts into my business account to address any   legitimate negative balance. 3. Alternatively, internally apply the necessary   amount toward the negative balance and release all remaining funds to me. 4.   Provide a complete accounting of every Citi account associated with me,   including all deposits, returned checks, debits, holds, offsets,   restrictions, transfers, and balances. 5. Identify the exact amount Citi   claims is necessary to bring the business account current. 6. Explain why   Citi will not allow the negative balance to be resolved using funds already   held in my Citi accounts. 7. Identify any legal, regulatory, or contractual   prohibition that Citi believes prevents such an internal transfer. 8. Explain   why Citi issued written correspondence indicating that the accounts would   reopen and then blocked the accounts again. 9. Identify any new evidence Citi   received after issuing the reopening correspondence. 10. Confirm the   substance of the three-way call in which XXXX verified that the HELOC check   was legitimate and authorized. 11. Provide the notes and records associated   with the approximately three-hour call involving Citi, XXXX, and me. 12.   Explain whether Citi continues to classify the transaction as fraud despite   XXXX confirmation. 13. Reimburse the interest, fees, and borrowing costs   arising from the emergency loan I was forced to obtain. 14. Reimburse   documented losses caused by the forced sale or pawning of my property. 15.   Correct or remove any inaccurate information Citi reported to XXXX XXXXXXXX   XXXX XXXX, credit-reporting agencies, fraud databases, or other financial   institutions. 16. Confirm whether Citi communicated with XXXX, XXXX, the   other HELOC borrower, or any other institution concerning my accounts. 17.   Provide copies of all closure notices, reopening notices, investigation   findings, account notes, fraud referrals, and nonprivileged records relied   upon in restricting my accounts. 18. Immediately release any funds exceeding   the legitimate amount necessary to resolve the business account balance. I   have made repeated good-faith attempts to resolve this matter. I participated   in an extensive fraud investigation, arranged direct verification from XXXX,   provided substantial outside funds, and repeatedly proposed a reasonable   internal transfer. Citi has rejected every reasonable solution while   continuing to retain approximately {$34000.00} of my money. I am requesting   immediate CFPB intervention because I have exhausted my personal resources   and can not continue borrowing or selling property merely to satisfy Citis   demand for outside funds while Citi refuses to make available the funds it   already holds.

text: In XX/XX/year>, a temporary authorization hold of 120 was placed on my   PayPal Cashback Mastercard account for a transaction that was later   identified as fraudulent. This transaction was only an authorization hold and   was never finalized or settled. The merchant fully released and refunded the   authorization, and no valid charge ever existed. Despite the transaction   being both fraudulent and refunded, Synchrony Bank, the issuer of the PayPal   Cashback Mastercard, incorrectly treated the authorization as a posted charge   and later processed it as a disputed transaction. This occurred even though   the merchant had already refunded the amount and there was no legitimate   debt. As part of this improper dispute handling, Synchrony charged PayPal for   the transaction. In turn, PayPal debited my PayPal balance approximately   {$140.00}, leaving my PayPal account with a negative balance, even though the   transaction was fraudulent, the merchant fully refunded the 120   authorization, the charge was never finalized or valid, and I do not owe this   amount to either institution. At the same time, Synchrony Bank has been   sending me recurring billing and past-due email notifications stating that I   owe money related to this same alleged debt, including late fees and interest.   However, Synchrony will not provide access to an actual billing statement.   When I click the links in these emails to view the bill online, I am   redirected to PayPal, where no Synchrony bill or statement is visible. I am   receiving payment demands and late-fee notices for a debt that I can not   view, verify, or reconcile. I have contacted both PayPal and Synchrony Bank   multiple times. Each institution refuses to resolve the issue and instead   directs me to the other. PayPal states the issue must be handled by Synchrony   Bank, while Synchrony Bank states the issue must be handled by PayPal. As a   consumer, I am being improperly charged and threatened with fees due to a   failure between two financial institutions to correctly handle a fraudulent   and refunded authorization and to provide required billing transparency. This   is not a valid debt. I am being asked to pay money that neither PayPal nor   Synchrony Bank is legally entitled to collect, and I am being assessed late   fees and interest without access to a proper billing statement. I am   requesting immediate removal of the negative balance from my PayPal account,   immediate cessation of all billing notices, late fees, and interest related   to this transaction, written confirmation that I do not owe this amount to   PayPal or Synchrony Bank, assurance that this matter will not be sent to   collections or reported negatively, and correction of all internal records   related to this transaction. I am filing this complaint because neither   PayPal nor Synchrony Bank has taken responsibility for correcting errors   arising from their internal fraud, dispute, settlement, and billing   processes, despite clear evidence that the transaction was fraudulent,   refunded, never finalized, and never resulted in a valid charge.
